subject: english
question: 作者論及一項新政策時寫道：「委員會自然沒有諮詢任何真正受影響的人。」語氣是甚麼？
questionEn: A writer says of a new policy: "Naturally, the committee consulted no one who would actually be affected." What is the tone?
options: Sarcastic — "naturally" marks disapproval of what is called expected
Neutral — the sentence merely reports what the committee actually did
Admiring — the writer commends the committee for acting so decisively
Uncertain — the writer does not know whether any consultation occurred
optionsEn: Sarcastic — "naturally" marks disapproval of what is called expected
Neutral — the sentence merely reports what the committee actually did
Admiring — the writer commends the committee for acting so decisively
Uncertain — the writer does not know whether any consultation occurred
explanation: 語氣由用詞承載，與內容同等重要。「自然」把「沒有諮詢」說成完全在意料之中，而把一項失職說成理所當然，正是一種譴責 —— 作者要表達的與贊同相反。這是說明文中反語的標準訊號：一個表示「意料之中」的標記（自然、當然、不出所料）配上一件讀者理應反感的事。中立報道會省去這個標記；讚賞需要正面評價，而文中並無；不確定則需要「似乎」「可能」一類的模糊語。
explanationEn: Tone is carried by word choice as much as by content. "Naturally" presents the failure to consult as entirely predictable, and treating a failure as predictable is a way of condemning it — the writer means the opposite of approval. This is the standard signal of sarcasm in expository prose: a marker of expectation ("naturally", "of course", "unsurprisingly") attached to something the reader is meant to find objectionable. A neutral report would omit the marker; admiration would need positive evaluation, which is absent; and uncertainty would need hedging such as "seems" or "may have".

subject: english
question: 下列哪一組詞語最可能顯示【審慎】而非斷言的語氣？
questionEn: Which set of words would most likely signal a CAUTIOUS rather than an assertive tone?
options: may, tends to, in some cases, appears to
must, always, undeniably, without exception
never, impossible, certainly, proves
urgent, alarming, catastrophic, immediately
optionsEn: may, tends to, in some cases, appears to
must, always, undeniably, without exception
never, impossible, certainly, proves
urgent, alarming, catastrophic, immediately
explanation: 審慎的作者會使用模糊限制語：情態動詞（may、might、could）、頻率限定（tends to、often）、範圍限定（in some cases、in this context）、以及證據標記（appears to、suggests）。這些詞語合起來表示：這項主張是「大概如此」而非「已成定論」。第二、三組作用相反，斷言普遍性與確定性。第四組傳達的是緊迫感，屬於語氣的另一個維度 —— 作者可以同時緊迫而審慎（「這可能相當嚴重，值得即時關注」），因此不應把緊迫讀成斷言。
explanationEn: A cautious writer hedges: modal verbs (may, might, could), frequency qualifiers (tends to, often), scope limiters (in some cases, in this context) and evidential markers (appears to, suggests). Together these signal that the claim is offered as probable rather than settled. The second and third sets do the opposite, asserting universality and certainty. The fourth conveys urgency, which is a different dimension of tone altogether — a writer can be urgent and cautious at once ("this may prove serious and warrants attention now"), so urgency should not be read as assertiveness.

subject: english
question: 一篇文章前三段稱讚一項計劃，然後列出三個未解決的問題。這個結構最可能反映作者的整體態度是甚麼？
questionEn: A passage praises a scheme in its first three paragraphs, then lists three unresolved problems. What does this structure most likely indicate about the writer's overall attitude?
options: Qualified support — favourable, but conditional on the problems being solved
Complete opposition — the praise was insincere and only the problems count
Complete support — the problems are raised purely as a formal gesture
Indifference — the writer holds no position on the scheme either way
optionsEn: Qualified support — favourable, but conditional on the problems being solved
Complete opposition — the praise was insincere and only the problems count
Complete support — the problems are raised purely as a formal gesture
Indifference — the writer holds no position on the scheme either way
explanation: 結構本身承載態度。把保留意見放在讚賞【之後】，等於讓它佔據結尾的位置，而在英文說明文之中，結尾位置通常份量較重，因此全文讀來是「有條件的支持」。把讚賞讀成虛偽、或把問題讀成例行公事，都無法解釋作者何以在兩邊都花了篇幅。應付整體態度題的方法有二：看兩邊各佔多少篇幅，以及看哪一邊佔據結尾 —— 答案通常是有保留的立場而非絕對的立場。
explanationEn: Structure carries attitude. Placing reservations AFTER the praise gives them the final position, which in English expository writing usually carries the greater weight, so the piece reads as support that has been made conditional. Neither reading the praise as insincere nor treating the problems as a formality accounts for the space given to both. In examinations, questions on overall attitude are best answered by asking two things: how much space each side receives, and which side occupies the final position — the answer is usually a qualified rather than an absolute stance.

subject: english
question: 文中寫道：「到第三週，診所外的人龍已經消失。」可以合理推斷甚麼？
questionEn: A text states: "By the third week, the queue outside the clinic had disappeared." What can be reasonably inferred?
options: Something changed demand or capacity, though the text does not say what
The clinic closed down permanently at the end of the second week of operation
Everyone in the district had recovered and no longer required any treatment
The clinic began turning patients away without treating any of them at all
optionsEn: Something changed demand or capacity, though the text does not say what
The clinic closed down permanently at the end of the second week of operation
Everyone in the district had recovered and no longer required any treatment
The clinic began turning patients away without treating any of them at all
explanation: 推斷必須由文本加上一般推理得出，並且到此為止。人龍消失，意味着來的人少了，或者服務速度快了，而文中並無交代成因 —— 因此站得住的推斷停在「有些東西改變了」，並列出兩種可能而不從中選一。其餘三項各自補上了文本並不支持的具體成因：結業、全區康復、拒絕診治。推斷題最常見的錯誤正是如此 —— 在文本只支持一個籠統結論之處，補上一個看似合理的故事。
explanationEn: An inference must follow from the text plus ordinary reasoning, and no further. A queue that disappears means either that fewer people came or that they were served faster, and the passage supplies neither cause — so the defensible inference stops at "something changed", naming the two possibilities without choosing between them. The other three options each supply a specific cause the text does not support: closure, universal recovery, or refusal of treatment. The commonest error in inference questions is exactly this — supplying a plausible story where the text supports only a general conclusion.

subject: english
question: 文本的「明言」與「暗示」有何分別？
questionEn: What is the difference between what a text STATES and what it IMPLIES?
options: A statement is written directly; an implication is drawn by the reader
A statement is true whereas an implication is always false or misleading
A statement appears early in a text and an implication only at the very end
They are the same thing, merely described using two different terms
optionsEn: A statement is written directly; an implication is drawn by the reader
A statement is true whereas an implication is always false or misleading
A statement appears early in a text and an implication only at the very end
They are the same thing, merely described using two different terms
explanation: 文本【明言】的內容寫在紙上，可以直接引用。【暗示】則須由讀者根據所寫、所略、以及表述方式建構出來 —— 一位作者詳述某政策的代價而只用一個短句帶過其好處，等於在沒有明言的情況下作出了判斷。暗示並非虛假：它只是通往意義的另一條路徑，而考試之所以考它，正因為粗心閱讀最容易在此出錯 —— 或漏掉一個暗示，或無中生有地讀出文本承載不起的暗示。位置先後與此無關，兩者亦絕非同義詞。
explanationEn: What a text STATES is on the page and can be quoted. What it IMPLIES must be constructed by the reader from what is written, what is omitted, and how it is phrased — a writer who describes a policy's cost in detail and its benefits in one clause implies a judgement without stating one. Implication is not falsehood: it is a different route to meaning, and one that examinations test because it is where careless reading goes wrong, either missing an implication or inventing one the text will not bear. Position in the text is irrelevant, and the two are certainly not synonyms.

subject: english
question: 學生答推斷題時寫下自己對該題目的個人看法。為何這通常得分很低？
questionEn: A student answers an inference question by writing what they personally believe about the topic. Why does this usually score poorly?
options: The answer must be traceable to the passage, not to the reader's own views
Personal opinion is always wrong, so it cannot earn any credit
The answer is too short, since opinions are briefer than inferences
Inference questions never have a correct answer, so any response is arbitrary
optionsEn: The answer must be traceable to the passage, not to the reader's own views
Personal opinion is always wrong, so it cannot earn any credit
The answer is too short, since opinions are briefer than inferences
Inference questions never have a correct answer, so any response is arbitrary
explanation: 推斷是一種受約束的閱讀：答案必須由文本推導得出，讀者可以帶入一般常識，但不可帶入個人信念。兩個對該題目意見相左的讀者，應該仍然得出相同的推斷，因為證據就是文本本身。寫下個人看法等於用自己的前提取代了文本的前提，答案因而無法追溯到所讀的內容。個人意見本身並無錯，在議論寫作中自有其位置；問題在於用在一項要求證據的任務上。長短與此無關，而推斷題確實有站得住的答案。
explanationEn: Inference is constrained reading: the answer must be derivable from the passage by a reader who brings general knowledge but not private conviction. Two readers who disagree about the topic should still reach the same inference, because the evidence is the text. Writing a personal view substitutes one's own premises for the passage's, so the answer becomes untraceable to what was read. Personal opinion is not wrong in itself and has its place in discursive writing; the fault is using it where the task requires evidence. Length is beside the point, and inference questions do have defensible answers.

subject: english
question: 在「委員會否決了該提案，因為它成本太高」一句中，「它」指甚麼？
questionEn: In "The committee rejected the proposal because it was too costly", what does "it" refer to?
options: The proposal — the nearest preceding noun that fits the sense
The committee — the subject of the main clause
The rejection — the action described by the verb
It refers to nothing specific and is used only for grammar
optionsEn: The proposal — the nearest preceding noun that fits the sense
The committee — the subject of the main clause
The rejection — the action described by the verb
It refers to nothing specific and is used only for grammar
explanation: 指代題的答法是把候選項同時放進【位置】與【意義】兩重檢驗。最接近的前置名詞是「該提案」，而意義上亦通：提案可以成本高，而委員會成本高並不能解釋否決。兩重檢驗不一致時以意義為準 —— 英文作者並不總是把代詞緊貼其指代對象。實用的做法是把候選項代回句中，看推理是否仍然成立。「否決」是動作而非句中的名詞；至於無所指的 it，出現在 it is raining 一類句式，並非此處。
explanationEn: Reference questions are answered by testing candidates against BOTH position and sense. The nearest preceding noun is "the proposal", and it also makes sense: a proposal can be costly, whereas a committee being costly would not explain a rejection. When the two tests disagree, sense governs — English writers do not always place a pronoun beside its referent. A useful check is to substitute the candidate back into the sentence and see whether the reasoning still holds. "The rejection" is an action rather than a noun in the sentence, and an empty "it" appears in constructions such as "it is raining", not here.

subject: english
question: 文中「the drug arrests the spread of infection」一句使用了 arrest 一詞。此處取哪一個意思？
questionEn: A passage uses the word "arrest" in "the drug arrests the spread of infection". Which meaning applies?
options: To stop or check a process from continuing
To take someone into custody by legal authority
To attract and hold someone's attention
To place under formal charge in a court of law
optionsEn: To stop or check a process from continuing
To take someone into custody by legal authority
To attract and hold someone's attention
To place under formal charge in a court of law
explanation: 詞義題考的是讀者會否讓【句子】決定詞義，而非直接取該詞最常見的意思。arrest 最常指拘捕，但此處它的受詞是「感染的擴散」，並不能被拘捕，而主語是藥物而非執法人員。此處所需的是較舊的一個義項 —— 使某個過程停止，這個用法在醫學寫作中仍然通行。方法始終一致：先看該詞支配甚麼、由甚麼發出，再選出這兩者容許的義項。有一項「吸引注意」是該詞的真實義項，但與此處的主語受詞不合。
explanationEn: Vocabulary-in-context questions test whether the reader lets the SENTENCE decide the meaning rather than reaching for the commonest sense of the word. "Arrest" most often means detention, but its object here is "the spread of infection", which cannot be detained, and the subject is a drug rather than an officer. The sense required is the older one of halting a process, still current in medical writing. The method is always the same: identify what the word governs and who or what performs it, then choose the sense those two permit. One option, arresting attention, is a real sense of the word but does not fit this subject and object.

subject: english
question: 為何單憑詞典釋義去答語境詞義題會有風險？
questionEn: Why is it risky to answer a vocabulary-in-context question using a dictionary definition alone?
options: A word may carry several senses, and only the context selects the right one
Dictionary definitions are frequently inaccurate and should not be trusted
Examiners require answers in the student's own words, never a definition
Words in reading passages never carry their dictionary meanings
optionsEn: A word may carry several senses, and only the context selects the right one
Dictionary definitions are frequently inaccurate and should not be trusted
Examiners require answers in the student's own words, never a definition
Words in reading passages never carry their dictionary meanings
explanation: 大部分常用英文詞都有多個義項，而詞典會把它們一併列出，並不會為某一個句子排出先後。直接取第一條，或取自己剛好認得的那條，正是這類題目失分的方式。可靠的做法是先讀前後文，推出該詞在此處必須是甚麼意思，文章才說得通，然後才回頭核對詞典是否有對應的義項。詞典並非不可靠，問題亦不在於措辭；有一項則說得過頭 —— 文章中的詞語通常確實用着詞典列出的某一個義項，只是未必是第一個。
explanationEn: Most common English words carry several senses, and a dictionary lists them all without ranking them for a particular sentence. Choosing the first entry, or the sense one happens to know, is precisely how such questions are failed. The reliable method is to read the surrounding sentences, work out what the word must mean for the passage to make sense, and only then check that a dictionary sense matches. Dictionaries are not unreliable, and the objection is not about phrasing; one option overstates the point, since words in passages usually do carry a listed sense — just not always the first one.
